- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if history shows volatility.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated overshoot in next 3–5 days; dampen forecast peaks following spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if history shows price oscillating, forecast often fails to capture sustained trend; align forecast with sentiment direction over 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts using 3–5 day moving average of sentiment-weighted history.
- For 30d forecasts, model often underestimates long-term trend (especially >15d) when sentiment is bullish; scale up forecast by 10–20% if sentiment >0.67 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is flat or negative over 5+ days, model tends to ignore underlying trend; force a slight upward bias if history shows upward momentum, or downward if sentiment is bearish.
